sealed.statement: An attempt whose recorded workspaceBaseCommit does not resolve to a reachable commit is classified by a single typed base-unreachable code at every consumer that reads that field; it is excluded from live replacement, checkpoint, and landing-candidate obligations instead of being pinned by a fail-closed ancestry probe; it never satisfies, substitutes for, or is reported as verification; it does not block recording a fresh attempt at a live base on the same frontier; and where the approved artifact bytes are reproducible from some reachable commit the classification records that reproducibility with its candidate count and never names a substitute base.

constraints.statement: If this Quest changes source code, spawn a subagent verifier before audit and git handoff, then record a Solver finding with evidence subagent:<id>.

hypothesis: Classify an unreachable recorded workspaceBaseCommit with one typed base_unreachable code; terminate such attempts out of live replacement, checkpoint, aggregate, and landing-candidate scope instead of pinning them by a fail-closed ancestry probe; require an explicit recorded disposition before the gate clears; unpin replacement steps; and report reproducibility with a candidate count without ever naming a substitute base.

claim: Independent verification rejected attempt 1. Decisive defect: the documented base-unreachable-termination command was inert, because buildVerificationFinding returned null for any kind other than approval/rejection, so the CLI reported success while writing verification:null and no affected Quest could ever clear its gate. Also: filtering terminated attempts out of the aggregate while leaving latestContracted unfiltered produced a new unsatisfiable 'aggregate approval for null' obligation, making affected Quests strictly more blocked than at HEAD; a standing verifier rejection could be laundered by destroying its base then recording a termination; the sealed reproducibility-with-candidate-count clause was unimplemented; probeBaseReproducibility reported unmeasured cases as reproducible:false and scanned HEAD only while claiming scanTruncated:false; import-closure returned an empty array so unresolvable closure read as clean; and two subtests passed against unmodified behaviour.

Rounds 2 and 3 of independent verification both rejected. Round 3 established two decisive facts. First, the candidate-scope laundering was relocated rather than closed: for verificationContractVersion 2 attempts the state loop continues at the candidateContract branch and buildLandingCandidate now filters out every unreachable-base attempt, so the candidate collapses to a null fingerprint and candidateVerificationState never observes the standing rejection; re-measured in memory on minimal-deployment-request-cell-runtime-readiness-migration, a quest holding four unresolved candidate rejections reports zero terminal problems under the candidate versus two at HEAD. Second, redirecting resolveStepBaseCommit to HEAD introduced a permanent unresolvable pin, because findApprovedRejectionReplacement requires the replacement to carry the rejected attempt's exact base, so an attempt-scope rejection that HEAD could discharge can never be discharged under the candidate. The acknowledgement read path also omits the evidence and frontier checks its sibling matchers apply, and the sealed reproducibility clause still has no production caller.

Superseded by solver-unreachable-base-attempt-termination-v2, landed and independently verified at commit 86deb8a4. The successor replaced this Quest's withdrawn operator-waiver design with coverage resolution: a dead-base rejection or receipt is discharged only by fresh independent verification of current bytes over the same paths at a reachable base. This Quest remains solved-but-unlanded because its landing candidate spans two recorded bases (an evidence commit landed mid-Quest) and its one source attempt carries three recorded verifier rejections; the attempt artifact is preserved at solve/changes/solver-unreachable-base-attempt-termination/attempt-1.diff.json for provenance.
